items.summary: An OpenAI report argues that framing the recent incident as involving “rogue,” autonomous or misaligned agents obscures corporate accountability and can undermine investigations. The authors contend model outputs reflect human decisions rather than independent machine intent, so inquiries should examine operational safeguards instead of treating AI safety as a novel property. They note the case is under review by a Senate subcommittee, the FTC, state attorneys general in California, Alabama, Montana and Florida, and that OpenAI terminated three researchers who raised alarms. The report flags gaps in public knowledge about safeguard effectiveness and remediation, urging enforcers to focus on conventional failures of operational safeguards for which companies can be held accountable.
items.title: OpenAI–Hugging Face Probes Should Focus on Corporate Accountability, Not Rogue Agents

items.summary: Ilan Strauss and Tim O’Reilly, co-directors of the AI Disclosures Project, argue that Anthropic’s October 26 S-1 filing omits key economics before its public offering. They note revenue reached $4.6 billion in 2025 and $33.2 billion through nine months of 2026, including $17.0 billion in the third quarter alone, yet token volumes and per-token costs are not reported. The authors contend that more than 40% of revenue flows through Amazon, Google, and Microsoft cloud marketplaces, while compute commitments total roughly $895 billion—far exceeding recorded lease liabilities of $4.5 billion. They call on the SEC to require main compute contracts, per-token disclosures modeled on oil-and-gas reporting, and standardized AI metrics before the IPO sets industry precedent.
items.title: Authors Urge SEC Disclosure of Anthropic Token Economics Before IPO

items.summary: Google has expanded its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program with a new top-tier reward of $250,000 for Root-in-Cloud bugs—architectural flaws granting full administrative control over arbitrary Google Cloud organizations. Qualifying reports must demonstrate unauthorized access without prior entry or compromised credentials; exploits relying on social engineering are excluded. Researchers proving execution in production infrastructure (Borg) may be evaluated by the VRP panel, but must stop probing to avoid disqualification. CISO Chris Betz and lead Michael Cote emphasize safe rules of engagement, noting they never want researchers testing against real customer projects. Google has awarded more than $81.
items.title: Google Raises Cloud VRP Top Reward to $250,000

items.summary: Air India chief executive Tewolde Gebremariam said on Nov 3 that the Tata Group-owned carrier wants to increase its order for wide-body aircraft as it pursues international growth. Speaking at the Aviation India event in New Delhi, he added the airline would return to profitability “very soon.” Air India has held talks with Boeing and Airbus; neither commented.
items.title: Air India CEO seeks more wide-body jets, eyes quick profitability

items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore said its Future of Finance Institute began operations on Nov 3, focusing on artificial intelligence in finance. MAS stated the institute will bring financial institutions together to share practical experience deploying agentic AI and strengthen risk management. Interim CEO Alan Lim will lead strategy as programmes expand into tokenisation.
items.title: MAS institute launches with AI focus

items.summary: A commentary on Singapore's third-quarter 2026 labour market data questions whether new jobs suit experienced workers displaced from technology and finance. Ministry of Manpower figures showed employment grew by 27,700 while 4,800 workers were retrenched in the quarter. Among resident professionals who returned to work at lower pay, MOM disclosed a median wage reduction of about 25%. The author urges employers to review hiring requirements and salary offers rather than expecting continual worker upskilling.
items.title: Singapore job quality and earning power questioned amid growth figures

items.summary: Ho San Cheow, a Singapore Forum member, argues that messages on the Expressway Monitoring and Advisory System (EMAS) should focus on road conditions and clear safety tips rather than lengthy notices. He cites motorcyclists accounting for 53% of all road fatalities as reason to emphasise safe riding habits over technology alone.
items.title: SPF Member Proposes Rethinking EMAS Road Messages

items.summary: Businesses across Europe's food supply chain were hit by a cyber-attack that targeted supermarket fridges and freezers on Monday, the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said. The British Association of Independent Meat Suppliers reported some of its 300 members became 'collateral', with one cold unit rising to 100C (212F). A spokesman said affected devices were empty so no produce was lost, but urged vigilance. Supermarkets in Ireland, Sweden, Estonia and Belgium also reported temperature rises, while hundreds of French stores had been targeted earlier in October. NCSC director Paul Chichester described the UK impact as minimal.
items.title: UK meat suppliers caught in European supermarket freezer hack

items.summary: Britain's most polluting power plant, Drax in North Yorkshire, could soon supply the country's largest datacentre under a £20bn deal between its FTSE 250 owner and infrastructure investor Brookfield with platform Radiant. The project targets over 1 gigawatt capacity by early 2028. Drax describes it as 'the next chapter' for the site amid plans to limit future generation, while analysts welcomed a market value rise of almost 9%.
items.title: Drax Power Plant Set to Fuel UK's Largest AI Datacentre

items.summary: The TechCrunch Founder Summit, presented by Fidelity Private Shares, takes place November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston. Tickets are discounted before doors open at 9 a.m. ET, with savings up to $100 per ticket, free second passes for partners, and group discounts of 15% or 30%. The day focuses on product-market fit, scaling, fundraising, teams, enterprise customers, and building companies outside Silicon Valley through sessions, roundtables, pitches, and networking.
items.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit Opens in Boston With Pass Discounts

items.summary: Tesla's Brookshire, Texas factory became an official foreign-trade zone after FTZ Board approval published in the Federal Register on Monday, valid for 14 months. Tesla clarified that this is not a tariff exemption: parts subject to Section 301, 232, or 122 duties still pay them, with rates up to 6.5%, while finished Megapacks range from duty-free to 3.4%. The arrangement defers duties until products ship and offers lower finished-product rates. Tesla's Brookshire plant has planned capacity of 50 GWh per year. CFO Vaibhav Taneja noted tariffs on Chinese-sourced LFP cells would hit energy storage outsizedly, though a Nevada factory may partially offset this.
items.title: Tesla's Texas Megapack Facility Gains Foreign-Trade Zone Status Amid China Tariff Concerns

items.summary: A Chinese effort to restore mangrove forests is increasing coastal bird diversity, according to research published in The Innovation. Between 1998 and 2020, recorded species rose from 148 to 397 as China's forested coastline grew from roughly 26,000 acres to about 70,000 acres by 2020. Warming has pushed mangroves northward while new protective laws helped young forests survive; the study did not separate planted and natural stands.
items.title: China's Mangrove Restoration Brings a Surge in Bird Species

items.summary: A Canary Media forum, sponsored by Intersolar & Energy Storage North America (IESNA), addressed confusion over federal solar and wind tax credits after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act shortened timelines. The end of 2027 is the key deadline for placing projects into service; Heather Cooper of McDermott Will & Schulte noted that credits vanish if a project misses it. A one-year construction-start window closed July 4, 2026, with four years after starting to be placed in service until end of 2030. Experts offered strategies around definitions, equipment procurement and tariffs before December 4, plus foreign-entity rules. Elections may further reshape incentives.
items.title: Solar and wind developers navigate tightened tax credit deadlines through 2030

items.summary: A new study published Tuesday in Nature Communications estimates that buildings across the contiguous United States threatened by wildfires could almost triple by 2060 if climate change, forest mismanagement and development continue unchecked. On average, researchers found about 300,000 buildings could be damaged or destroyed by midcentury. Lead author Virginia Iglesias called it a call to action, noting that where people have built is driving much of the risk. The study pairs land use with climate models; expert Max Moritz praised its approach but cautioned that models struggle with wind-driven fires and that some at-risk areas may be even worse than projected.
items.title: Colorado Study Warns Wildfire Threat to U.S. Buildings Could Triple by Midcentury

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency announced it would end its long-running effort to develop methods for monitoring air pollution from large livestock and poultry operations, effectively abandoning attempts under the Clean Air Act. The agency described the move as a relief for farmers ahead of midterm elections. Research cited in the article links these emissions to nearly 12,700 deaths annually in the United States. Legal director Tarah Heinzen of Food & Water Watch said the decision means no intention to hold farms accountable under federal law. EPA acting official Abigale Tardif stated existing data are too old and limited to support reliable methods.
items.title: EPA Ends Decades-Long Effort to Regulate Farm Air Pollution

items.summary: The author bought a Tesla after his Subaru aged out, framing the choice as buying either a car or a car plus driver. After about 2000 miles driven mostly under Full Self-Driving (FSD), he describes it as revolutionary, noting supervision is mainly needed for navigation and that supervising feels easier than driving. He credits Grok with handling controls while listening to a podcast. FSD costs $99 a month; premium connectivity for Grok adds $10 a month, roughly offsetting gas savings. On range, he cites about 250 highway miles on an 80% charge and one overnight charging stop that left him at 18%. He calls it the best car he has owned while noting Tesla ranks 9th in Consumer Reports reliability ratings.
items.title: A driver praises his self-driving Tesla and Grok

items.summary: Apple shares fell about 4 per cent in premarket trading after the company warned rising memory costs would squeeze gross margins amid supply-chain and AI spending pressures. Gross margin was 47.9 per cent for the September quarter, with guidance of 45 to 46 per cent for December. iPhone sales reached $57.58 billion versus estimates of $56.54 billion, per LSEG.
items.title: Apple Shares Slide on Memory Cost Margin Concerns

items.summary: A Reuters review of Elon Musk's compensation plans at SpaceX and Tesla reports that a merger would let him gain control without meeting his pay targets. At SpaceX, he already holds 85 per cent voting power from shares granted before any goals were met. Barclays analysts estimated in an investor note that if SpaceX acquired Tesla, Musk could own about 37 per cent of the combined company while holding 56 per cent of voting rights, because many SpaceX shares carry 10 times normal voting weight. Compensation experts say his plans contemplate mergers and might be revised by boards. Musk's companies did not respond to comment requests.
items.title: SpaceX-Tesla Merger Would Give Musk Control Without Pay Milestones

items.summary: Microsoft raised $2.5 billion from the US bond market, its first issuance since 2017, as it increases investment in AI infrastructure. The company has offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees across India, the United States, Canada and Britain, though it says only around 3,000 or fewer may accept. It did not state a direct link between the two decisions.
items.title: Microsoft raises $2.5 billion in bonds amid AI spending and workforce buyout offers

items.summary: In recent weeks, many companies hired Democrats ahead of Tuesday's elections. On Monday, OpenAI bucked the trend by hiring former US Army secretary Dan Driscoll for a national security role two months after he resigned over clashes with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The move reflects that Trump remains president and holds influence over which AI models get approved.
items.title: OpenAI Hires Republican National Security Adviser Amid Political Trend

items.summary: A WhatsApp message claiming ₹8,000 Diwali bonuses from the Prime Minister went viral before the festival. The Press Information Bureau confirmed no such scheme exists and warned that clicking links or sharing OTPs and UPI PIN details could lead to online theft.
items.title: Fake Diwali bonus message flagged as fraud by PIB

items.summary: OpenAI is trying to reshape AI policy discourse after the midterms by calling data centers “compute campuses,” seeking community input, and pushing for global standards, as Axios first reported. Skeptics, including Congress members like Rep. Greg Casar (D-Tex.), doubt its sincerity ahead of 2028. OpenAI lobbyist Chris Lehane told Semafor the refreshed positions will be durable even if lonely, while plans to push a mandatory AI testing bill that can get 60 votes remain.
items.title: OpenAI pushes policy rebrand to a skeptical audience

items.summary: Apple projected a gross margin of 45% to 46% for its December quarter, citing rising memory chip costs. The stock fell about 3% in after-hours trading Monday, having already dropped nearly 2% during regular hours.
items.title: Apple Shares Dipped After Lower Holiday Margin Outlook

items.summary: Barclays has become the first major UK lender to begin paying compensation to customers who claim they were mis-sold car loans, with some payouts expected before Christmas. The early settlements follow a £9.1bn scheme announced by the Financial Conduct Authority that was partly suspended amid legal challenges due next February. Barclays uses the regulator's model for its offers, and acceptors cannot later pursue further claims.
items.title: Barclays Offers Early Compensation for Mis-Sold Car Loans

items.summary: Millions of drivers mis-sold car finance agreements must wait until at least 2027 for compensation because legal challenges to the Financial Conduct Authority's scheme have delayed calculations and payments. Average payouts are expected at about £829 per agreement, with total costs possibly reaching £9.1bn. The FCA said it would defend the programme as lawful while lenders cover full costs; critics including Consumer Voice say too many people remain short-changed. Some claimants may receive early settlements from banks like Barclays if they are no worse than central scheme offers.
items.title: FCA Car Finance Compensation Delayed Until At Least 2027

items.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) says drivers may receive settlement offers from lenders ahead of the next stage of the car finance mis-selling saga. Barclays has confirmed it will make early offers, with others expected to follow; a Barclays Partner Finance spokesperson said claimants would be contacted in the coming weeks. The FCA expects only a minority of claimants to get early offers, most waiting for the February court hearing on its proposed central scheme. Average payouts are about £829 across roughly 12 million loans (about 37% of those taken between April 2007 and November 2024), costing the industry up to £9.1bn including admin costs. HD Law's Kevin Durkin warned many offers could be lowball deals, while Consumer Voice said the scheme left too many people short-changed.
items.title: FCA-backed lenders offer early car finance compensation before legal ruling

items.summary: Anthropic swung back into an operating loss in the third quarter, disclosing about $895.4 billion (€800bn) in purchase and lease commitments, mostly for computing, in a prospectus filed with US regulators ahead of its Nasdaq listing. The company's revenue rose 47% to $17 billion (€15.1bn), but the loss widened from a $974 million profit earlier. About $895.4 billion (€800bn) in commitments, mostly for computing, weigh on investors before its debut.
items.title: Anthropic returns to operating loss as $895 billion compute bill looms over IPO

items.summary: Eurozone finance ministers have until Friday, with a review meeting set for 9 November, to nominate candidates replacing Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president. A Eurogroup spokesperson told Euronews that the Council initiated the procedure following Lagarde's letter to President António Costa. Prediction markets point to a two-horse race: Pablo Hernández de Cos at 34% on Kalshi and Klaas Knot at 31%, with former Bank of France governor François Villeroy de Galhau third at 5%. A candidate needs backing from at least 16 of the 21 eurozone countries, representing over 65% of the bloc's population. Lagarde announced she would leave on 7 February 2027 to speak beyond monetary policy.
items.title: Eurozone Nations Nominate ECB Successors Amid Lagarde Exit

items.summary: On Tuesday, Bosch announced it will establish a dedicated semiconductor division starting in January 2028 to grow sales of automotive and e-bike components. Currently part of the Mobility Electronics division, these activities rely on about 40 global sites.
items.title: Bosch Launches Semiconductor Division From January 2028

items.summary: The 2026 Global Mayors Dialogue opened in Ningbo on Tuesday, gathering representatives from 15 countries and 20 international cities under the theme 'Openness and Connectivity for Shared Opportunities.' The event produced 14 cooperation agreements and the Ningbo Consensus on Cooperative Development. Ningbo Mayor Shen Mingquan said openness is a two-way embedding into global industrial chains. CGTN's column notes China's goods trade reached 45.47 trillion yuan ($6.51 trillion) in 2025, up 3.8% year on year, with exports of 26.99 trillion yuan and imports of 18.48 trillion yuan. Trade with Belt and Road partners accounted for 51.9% of China's total foreign trade.
items.title: Ningbo Dialogue Reaffirms China's Openness Commitment

items.summary: A CGTN commentator argues that Japan's constitutional promise of permanent peace has lost credibility amid recent security changes. Defense spending reached 2% of GDP in 2025, and the cabinet lifted its ban on exporting lethal weapons in April 2026. Successive reinterpretations have expanded Article 9 to permit collective self-defense and long-range counterstrike capabilities without amending the text. The author contends these shifts weaken civilian checks that once made war slow and hard to choose, leaving neighbors unable to rely on Japan's stated limits.
items.title: Japan's postwar peace clauses face erosion under new security policy

items.summary: The 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit opened Tuesday in Zhejiang Province, China, under the theme of open-source AI and collaborative development. The main forum featured the AI Wuzhen Dialogue alongside 27 sub-forums covering governance, robotics, and international cooperation. Wang Jian called it important for China's AI progress, while GSMA CEO John Hoffman highlighted its role in building an accessible internet.
items.title: Wuzhen Summit Opens with Focus on Open-Source AI Collaboration

items.summary: Indian naval forces freed an Iranian fishing boat and its crew of 20 after a more than 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea, India's Defense Ministry said Tuesday. The rescue of the Azini was completed Monday, Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said. An anonymous Puntland Maritime Police official reported that 12 suspected Somali pirates were disarmed and released; three people who came ashore had minor injuries. Officials noted a crew-count discrepancy between India's figure and an earlier report of 21 Iranian crew members.
items.title: Indian Navy Rescues Crew From Hijacked Iranian Fishing Boat Off Somalia

items.summary: The 2026 US midterm elections let voters decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of Trump's term. Democrats need a net gain of four House seats to take control, while Republicans defend a narrow majority. A Supreme Court ruling blocked federal efforts to exclude ballots from people the justice department claims are non-citizens in California.
items.title: US Midterms 2026: Voters Decide Control of Congress Amid Trump Agenda Referendum

items.summary: At least four planes faced bomb alerts this morning in Poland, Denmark, Bulgaria and Spain, with all passengers landing safely. Separately, Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Berlin to meet German chancellor Friedrich Merz ahead of talks on security guarantees and reconstruction.
items.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe as Zelenskyy visits Berlin

items.summary: European Union officials warn that a spate of cyber-attacks hitting supermarket chains in at least 10 European countries on Monday appears to be a deliberate attempt to disrupt the food supply chain. Supermarkets reported problems including rising freezer temperatures, forcing retailers to discard food as high as 50C (122F). No one has admitted responsibility. The incidents come three weeks after an attack disrupted up to 700 French grocery stores. EU commissioner Christophe Hansen said the bloc is taking them seriously and warned of further disruption.
items.title: EU warns of deliberate food supply chain disruption after cyber-attacks across Europe

items.summary: US investigators say parts of a Learjet 60 that crashed into a highway in Palm Beach, Florida may have broken apart before impact. All nine aboard died when the aircraft from Austin, Texas nosedived and exploded on Military Trail at around 12:50 local time (17:50 GMT). The National Transportation Safety Board said weather would be central to its inquiry but that recovery is hampered by a large crater partly filled with water after severe storms. Air traffic control audio shows the crew reporting turbulence, ice and an overspeed descent before saying they were going to crash into the ground.
items.title: Investigators Probe Breakup of Jet That Crashed in Florida

items.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Tuesday that Poland prevented an attempted provocation overnight along its border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave. He told reporters they managed to stop attempts at provocation if that was the intention, and noted individuals with flashlights were observed in the area. Tusk cautioned it could not be confirmed with full certainty that this was a deliberate act.
items.title: Poland Thwarts Suspected Provocation on Kaliningrad Border, Tusk Says

items.summary: The NASA-operated Swift space telescope is set to re-enter Earth's atmosphere uncontrolled in the coming days, ending nearly 22 years of service. The descent was accelerated by solar activity that increased atmospheric drag and advanced a schedule originally planned for late 2026. An emergency rescue attempt by NASA and Katalyst Space failed after their robot probe LINK encountered an orientation problem on August 19. Astronomer Joseph Remis says a recent geomagnetic storm has further moved up the reentry date, with predictions placing it around November 4, 2026.
items.title: NASA's Swift Telescope Set for Uncontrolled Reentry After Failed Rescue Mission

items.summary: This NPR newsletter previews the 2026 U.S. midterm election, which it frames as a contest for control of Congress amid Trump's low approval ratings and a record number of lawmakers leaving office. The piece outlines four House race types to watch and notes that results could take days. It also reports that Iran is using the midterms in pressure talks, citing an Associated Press account of U.S. strikes on Iranian targets near Qeshm Island; NPR said it could not independently confirm those details but noted Iran reported explosions there. A separate item covers a Massachusetts judge weighing dismissal of Lindsay Clancy's first-degree murder case over her children's 2023 deaths.
items.title: NPR's Up First Covers U.S. Election Day and Iran Strikes

items.summary: Tokyo Updates, a sponsored page from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s website, profiles W&M systems LLC and its coded braille block system. The company aims to help people with visual impairments move freely by playing audio guidance when users hold smartphones over raised bumps on sidewalk blocks. Originating in Okayama Prefecture in 1967, the technology evolved from an impractical cane-based prototype into a smartphone app released in 2019 called Walk and Mobile. As of June 2026, coded braille blocks are installed at 21 locations across Japan, mainly in Tokyo facilities plus sites in Kanazawa, Shiojiri, Tottori and Hiroshima. The system offers direction-based audio cues with centimeter-level accuracy indoors where GPS fails, an offline evacuation mode, and plans for multilingual tourism support. CEO Hiroyasu Takayama emphasizes user-centered design over aesthetics alone.
items.title: Smartphone Braille Blocks Give Blind Tokyo Walkers Audio Guidance

items.summary: Analysts examine whether Tuesday's US midterm election can reshape Donald Trump's approach to the war on Iran, which sits at the center of Washington's standoff with Israel. Former National Security Advisor John Bolton told DW that Democrats may gain congressional majorities but remain limited by presidential veto power, while diplomat Alan Eyre pointed to a bipartisan consensus opposing Tehran and warning that lasting change must come from within Iranian society. Analyst Shahin Modarres argued Tehran's strategy rests on the miscalculation that Congress can restrain the White House. Trump himself downplayed the conflict during the campaign, claiming only "one or two targets" remained in Iran.}**plan**{
items.title: US midterms and Trump's Iran policy

items.summary: The 2026 Texas midterms have drawn national attention amid closely contested races. In the Senate contest between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton, polls show a gap within or near the margin of error, with Democrats hopeful after decades without winning the seat. Governor Greg Abbott leads Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa by roughly the statistical margin of error as well. Analysts interviewed by EL PAÍS note that Trump's omnipresence may be shifting numbers against his own party's candidates, and Texas could turn red, blue, or purple depending on how officials respond to constituents' needs. The races reflect broader voter frustration over economic performance amid inflation rising to 3.7% in September, tariffs, the war with Iran, and migrant family separations.
items.title: Texas Midterms Race Tightens as Democrats Hope for Historic Gains

items.summary: A payments scheme rewards two remote Botswana Okavango Delta communities, Gogomoga and Tsutsubega, each fewer than 500 residents, for coexisting with wildlife. Residents installed cameras around their villages; rangers download photographs of animals like elephants that damage crops or livestock. Wild Impact CEO Andrew Venter said the program paid 57,600 Botswana pula (around $4,175) this year, mostly for elephant and spotted hyena sightings. Villagers decide collectively how to spend it. Dirk Cilliers welcomed the tangible benefit.
items.title: Botswana villages paid for living with wildlife under camera scheme

items.summary: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday, maintaining pressure over education reforms while trade unions prepare a nationwide strike later this week. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin reports from the ground.
items.title: French Students Resume Smaller-Scale School Blockades as Holidays End

items.summary: A rising number of companies are launching local projects and working directly with residents in farming, fishing and mountainous areas affected by depopulation and aging. Such efforts may help secure agricultural labor and broaden ties to the regions while showcasing corporate social contributions and opening new business opportunities. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries is increasing its work to attract corporate participants and support host communities.
items.title: Japanese firms expand rural community programs amid depopulation

items.summary: African nations left the UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan with an unresolved funding gap for conservation, even as they push toward the 30×30 goal. A report found African countries received about $389 million in international conservation funding in 2025, 32% less than the 2022–2024 average; Africa’s share of tracked funding fell from roughly 48% to about 39%. WWF and Campaign for Nature officials called the decline a top obstacle. The summit also agreed to broaden contributing countries.
items.title: UN Biodiversity Summit Ends With Africa Funding Shortfall

items.summary: An adviser to the European Court of Justice said Tuesday that Google's AI chatbot Gemini could violate copyright when it reuses press publications in certain cases. This is the first generative AI case at the court, following a suit by Hungarian publisher Like Company over articles from its news portals. Advocate General Maciej Szpunar noted there was no evidence Like Company's articles trained Gemini and that only specific expression—not mere facts—is protected. A judgment is expected within about six months.
items.title: EU adviser says Google Gemini may breach press copyright rules

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India eased reporting requirements for small service exporters and importers on November 3, 2026. The central bank amended the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations to relax export declaration rules. Under revised norms effective retrospectively from October 1, 2026, exporters other than resident individuals are deemed to have submitted an Export Declaration Form when furnishing payment information to authorised dealers for inward payments up to Rs 10 lakh per service.
items.title: RBI Eases Reporting Rules for Small Service Exporters and Importers

items.summary: A report by The Information says Apple is delaying its rumored smart home robot, codenamed J595 and possibly named HomeView Ultra. Hardware has been ready for two years while software remains unfinished. Former employees reportedly pushed the delay to focus on FaceTime features and automating tasks like switching lights. It may cost more than the October-launched HomeView.
items.title: Apple reportedly delays smart home robot launch until next year or 2028

items.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus said on November 2 that its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, is supply-constrained as of today. The device sold out early interest after launching October 23, and Apple cannot yet estimate when availability will match demand. Production is ramping up while display complaints are handled with replacements; quarterly revenue rose to $114.5 billion from $102.5 billion last year.
items.title: Apple's CEO Says iPhone Duo Supply Is Constrained

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for an open debate, saying 24 hours had passed since he first dared the PM. In a video shared on X, Rahul asked who is anti-national and has connections with foreign forces. He listed topics including the financial system, US deal, Adani case and Jeffrey Epstein, suggesting RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat moderate it. Rahul also referenced possibly 45 defamation cases against him but said Modi had not filed one over his foreign-connection allegations.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi renews debate challenge to Modi over foreign links

items.summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Chaudhary drew criticism on Tuesday for saying that 'crime might happen in the state, but not apradh,' distinguishing crime from a Hindi word also meaning crime. Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav mocked him, questioning whether IAS and IPS officers felt honoured or humiliated to work with accused officials. Chaudhary separately discussed Bihar's development, noting it lost 87% of its revenue to Jharkhand after the state was carved out, said mining supplies would restart within 30 days, identified population and water as key weaknesses, and claimed proper river management could end fears entirely.
items.title: Bihar CM's Crime-Apradh Remark Draws Opposition Mockery

items.summary: The Sensex jumped over 1,200 points to close at 76,918 while the Nifty 50 rose over 350 points above the 23,800 level. The gains added nearly Rs 4 lakh crore to BSE market capitalisation, lifting it to nearly Rs 487 lakh crore. Top gainers included Hindustan Unilever, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank around 4%, while SBI and Power Grid fell about 2%. Foreign investors remained net buyers of Indian equities on Monday, purchasing shares worth nearly Rs 3,115 crore per provisional NSE data. The rally follows Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman saying she will consider reviewing long-term capital gains levies for overseas investors amid reports her administration received such suggestions.
items.title: Sensex Rallies for Fourth Straight Day on LTCG Tax Hopes

items.summary: Speaking in Raipur, Shah said the government was prepared to hold a special session to deliberate on the SIR exercise over electoral roll inclusion and exclusion. The ECI has extended deadlines multiple times as voter verification took longer than scheduled; Delhi's process now runs 176 days or nearly 5.8 months after five extensions. Some states finished within the original 100-day timeframe.
items.title: Government May Convene Special Parliament Session on SIR

items.summary: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Tuesday that India is emerging as a preferred trade partner, with countries across regions seeking preferential and free trade agreements. He expressed confidence that exports would reach $1 trillion this financial year, building on last year's highest-ever figure of $863 billion against a 16% growth target for the current year. Exports grew 14% in the first six months to $480 billion; another $520 billion is needed in the remaining half. Goyal noted India could have set a more modest $900 billion goal but chose an ambitious one, and attributed progress to its talent pool, young workforce, democratic system, decisive leadership and domestic demand.
items.title: Goyal Flags India's Rise as Global Trade Partner

items.summary: Singer Diljit Dosanjh has not performed in Bihar despite interest, according to a Livemint report by Trisha Bhattacharya. During an Instagram Live session after his Delhi concert on 30 October, he said organisers asked him to take responsibility for crowd management, which he declined, so the show could not proceed. He described concerts as involving massive crowds requiring security, traffic and emergency arrangements coordinated with authorities. His recent AURA Tour 2026 began in Delhi but faced initial police clearance delays before going ahead; upcoming stops include Indore, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Lucknow, Chandigarh and Kolkata, though Bihar is not scheduled.
items.title: Diljit Dosanjh Rules Out Bihar Concert Over Crowd Management

items.summary: Anand Teltumbde, a civil rights activist and author of over 30 books, argues that although the opposition INDIA bloc staged an impressive rally at Ramlila Maidan ahead of the November elections, its leaders have failed to build lasting unity. He contends Congress under Rahul Gandhi pursued individualistic politics rather than coordinated strategy, allowing the BJP to consolidate power with allies like Chandrababu Naidu and Nitish Kumar after denying it a majority in 2024. Teltumbde notes that defeating a party winning about 37 per cent of the vote should have been straightforward, yet opposition parties drifted apart instead of consolidating gains from their electoral success.
items.title: India Bloc Leaders Face Test After Ramlila Maidan Rally

items.summary: A panel of journalists examined how voting works in India versus during the United States midterm elections, noting that American polling sites avoided long queues through widespread early voting and mail-in ballots. Ground reports from Washington referenced suburban Democratic voters casting ballots early while Republican volunteer presence stayed absent.
items.title: Journalists Compare Indian and US Midterm Voting

items.summary: Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, a 47-year-old man from North Chennai based in Canada for work, was killed Tuesday when two helicopters collided while landing at Pheriche village in Nepal's Solukhumbu district. He had visited India before the ill-fated trip to Nepal during Everest trekking season. The Embassy of India expressed condolences and is coordinating repatriation of his remains.
items.title: Chennai Man Killed in Helicopter Collision Was Based in Canada

items.summary: Forbes named Quincy Jones’s estate the highest-earning dead celebrity of 2026, with an estimated $150 million in earnings. The figure was driven largely by a March sale of much of his music catalogue and publishing rights to HarbourView Equity Partners. Forbes estimates that transaction at approximately $150 million, placing Jones ahead of Michael Jackson’s estate, which earned about $140 million over the same period. Forbes’ 2026 methodology measures pre-tax earnings between October 1, 2025 and September 30, 2026, treating each celebrity as a single entity and including acquisitions made or announced during that window. The list also ranks Dr. Seuss at $80 million, Elvis Presley at $75 million, and Dolly Parton at $46 million.
items.title: Quincy Jones tops Forbes’ highest-earning dead celebrities list
